historical.text: Founder of the Maratha polity. His birth year is given as 1630 in many modern accounts and 1627 in others, so his exact age in 1646-1649 is uncertain. His reputation for mobility and use of hill forts is well established in the literature; the numeric bonuses here are gameplay values only.
sources: Mehendale, Gajanan B. Shivaji: His Life and Times

historical.text: Best documented as the defender of Chakan during the 1660 Mughal siege, which is outside this scenario's dates. His role and loyalties in 1646-1649 are uncertain, so placing him with the player here is a gameplay assumption, not a statement of history.
sources: Sarkar, Jadunath. Shivaji and His Times

historical.text: FICTIONAL PLACEHOLDER. This is not a historical person. It stands in for the Adil Shahi officers whose specific identities and dates in this campaign are not modelled here.

Bijapur noble and general who led the 1659 expedition against Shivaji and is said to have died at Pratapgad in November 1659. His role in the expedition is well attested; the details of the meeting and its outcome are heavily shaped by later tradition and differ between accounts.
sources: Sarkar, Jadunath. Shivaji and His Times

historical.text: Associated in the literature with command of Shivaji's cavalry from the mid-1650s. His specific role in the events of 1659 is uncertain, so his assignment here is a gameplay assumption.
sources: Sarkar, Jadunath. Shivaji and His Times

historical.text: Adil Shahi commander associated with the 1660 siege of Panhala. His appearance in a campaign that starts in 1659 is a gameplay compression of events across 1659-60.
sources: Sarkar, Jadunath. Shivaji and His Times

historical.text: Peshwa from 1720 until his death in 1740, remembered for fast-moving campaigns. The victory at Palkhed (1728) is often cited as an example. Numeric bonuses are gameplay values.
Younger brother of Baji Rao I, associated with campaigns including the Konkan and Vasai operations. His exact role in this scenario is a gameplay assignment.
Maratha commander who rose in Baji Rao I's service and is associated with Malwa. His placement here is a gameplay assumption.
Founder of the Asaf Jahi Deccan state. He was a leading opponent of Baji Rao I at Palkhed (1728) and Bhopal (1737-38).
sources: Eaton, Richard M. A Social History of the Deccan, 1300-1761 (Cambridge, 2005)

historical.text: FICTIONAL PLACEHOLDER, not a historical person. It stands in for Mughal provincial officers whose identities are not modelled.
The last Peshwa (ruled 1796-1818). He surrendered in June 1818 and the office was ended. His gameplay modifiers are neutral; no judgement of his generalship is intended.
Senior commander of the Peshwa's army in 1817-18, killed at Ashti in February 1818.
Bhonsle ruler of Nagpur in 1817, associated with the fighting at Sitabuldi in November 1817.
Holkar ruler whose army was defeated at Mahidpur in December 1817.
East India Company officer prominent in the 1817-18 campaign in Central India and in the Peshwa's surrender.
FICTIONAL PLACEHOLDER, not a historical person. It stands in for the Company officers who led field columns in 1817-18.
